prerequisites: Python Programming, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Computer Vision (CV)
description: Understand the fundamental concepts of emotions, emotion theories, and affective computing. Explore emotion recognition techniques using text, speech, facial expressions, physiological signals, and multimodal data. Design and evaluate AI-based models for emotion recognition using modern machine learning and deep learning techniques. Analyze the ethical, privacy, fairness, and societal implications of affective computing while exploring its real-world applications.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Affective Computing
syllabus.body: Human emotion recognition, interpretation, and simulation, history and evolution, emotion theories and models, emotion representation and annotation, experimental design, affect elicitation, research and development tools.

syllabus.title: Emotion in Text and Voice
syllabus.body: Emotion analysis from text, sentiment analysis, traditional and contextual word embeddings, transformer-based language models for emotion detection (BERT, RoBERTa, LLMs); speech emotion recognition, acoustic features: MFCC, pitch, energy, prosody, spectrogram features, CNN, CNN-LSTM, transformer models, self-supervised speech models.

syllabus.title: Emotion in Facial Expressions and Physiological Signals
syllabus.body: Facial Action Coding System (FACS), face detection, facial landmarks detection, face alignment, CNN-based recognition, vision transformers, micro-expression recognition, cross-domain facial emotion recognition; physiological signals analysis: EEG, ECG, EMG, GSR, HRV, wearable sensors.

syllabus.title: Advanced Topics and Ethical Issues
syllabus.body: Multimodal emotion recognition, emotion-aware and empathetic intelligent agents and social robots, real-time online and adaptive recognition of emotions, ethical legal and social implications; case studies: smart healthcare, mental health support, education and autism therapy, human-robot interaction, explainable AI for emotion recognition, edge AI for emotion recognition, generative AI in affective computing.

outcomes: Explain the fundamental concepts, theories of human emotions, and principles of affective computing.
Apply machine learning and deep learning techniques to recognize emotions from text, speech, facial expressions, and physiological signals.
Develop and evaluate unimodal and multimodal emotion recognition systems using modern AI techniques.
Analyze ethical, privacy, fairness, and societal challenges associated with affective computing applications.
textbooks: Rosalind W. Picard, Affective Computing, MIT Press.
Rafael A. Calvo and Sidney D'Mello, The Oxford Handbook of Affective Computing.
referenceBooks: Christopher Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning.
Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing.
Richard Szeliski, Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications.
